text: Why did a painter plant bamboo outside his window? His answer gave China one of its best-known sayings.
The saying has four characters: chest, have, finished, bamboo. A finished bamboo, already inside your chest.
Nearly a thousand years ago, in the Northern Song dynasty, the painter Wen Tong was famous for ink bamboo that looked alive.
His secret was not in the brush. He planted bamboo outside his window and watched it grow, in rain and sunshine, through every season.
So when he finally painted, he worked with ease. Before you paint bamboo, he said, you must first have the finished bamboo in your mind.
His cousin, the poet Su Shi, recorded this idea in an essay about one of Wen Tong's bamboo paintings. And the phrase lived on.
Today it means having a well-thought-out plan before you act, so you can move with calm confidence.
For example: facing this complex negotiation, he already had a well-prepared plan in mind.
Use it to describe someone who stays calm and certain, because their strategy is already fully mapped out.
The lesson: observe closely, plan ahead, and confidence follows. Like Wen Tong, have the bamboo ready before you paint.
